name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 9, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by members of Lion’s Heart.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY ACTING DEPUTY FIRE CHIEF
BENNETT

MAYOR SCHMITZ and the City Council thanked Chief Bennett for his years of service to
the City of Rolling Hills Estates and congratulated him on his new position as Acting Deputy
Fire Chief.

Los Angeles County Fire Assistant Chief Brian Kane introduced himself to the City Council
and community.

B. PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL 2024 AS EARTHQUAKE PREPAREDNESS
MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ declared April 2024 as Earthquake Preparedness Month.

C.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL 2024 AS DMV/DONATE LIFE MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ declared April 2024 as DMV/Donate Life Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-J AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MARCH & APRIL2024

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 9, 2024
   APPROVED WARRANTS 67190 THROUGH 67261 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $698,823.82 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 030124 THROUGH
  030524; IN THE AMOUNT OF $223,005.45 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $921,829.27 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORTS OF FEBRUARY 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF FEBRUARY 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 12, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF MARCH 26, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 22, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 6, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.
I.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MARCH 19, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

J.  RESOLUTION NO. 2568 CONTINUING THE PROCLAMATION OF THE LOCAL
  EMERGENCY ARISING FROM SIGNIFICANT LAND MOVEMENT ALONG AND IN
  THE VICINITY OF PEARTREE LANE IN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2568 CONTINUING THE PROCLAMATION
  OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY CAUSED BY SIGNIFICANT LAND MOVEMENT
  ON PEARTREE LANE.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  ARBOR DAY COMMEMORATION - SEAN BENNETT, BENNETT LANDSCAPE

Sean Bennett of Bennett Landscape announced that there will be a tree planting ceremony in
honor of Arbor Day at City Hall on April 23, 2024.

Written public comment was received from Brandee Keith of South Coast AQMD reminding
residents that May marks the start of ozone season and that it is common for air quality to
reach unhealthy levels in the afternoon hours. The AQMD app and website have resources
and more information available for the public.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

None.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CITY WORK PLAN 2023/24 QUARTERLY UPDATE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 9, 2024
   Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the report.

City Manager Greg Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Manager Grammer explained that the Pepper Tree Foundation Fundraising Committee
would be meeting next week to finalize things before launching a fundraising campaign for
the George F Canyon Nature Center project in May or June, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA noted that these goals are now publicly presented as
suggested by the City Manager, giving the public an opportunity to see what the City is focused
on and working on.

City Council consensus to receive and file this report.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Cal Cities Housing, Community, and Economic
Development (HCED) meeting this month in-person in Burbank, as well as the Cal Cities
Los Angeles Division meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN attended this month’s Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) Community, Economic & Human Development Committee meeting.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Government’s
General Assembly along with COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR SCHMITZ attended the Palos Verdes Realtors Association’s Legislative Breakfast
where each Mayor provided a State of the City.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Palo Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s
Legislative Action Committee meeting earlier today, as well as the Neighborhood Council
meeting last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN announced the upcoming SCAG Regional Conference &
General Assembly May 2-3 and the California Contract Cities Association’s (CCCA) Annual
Municipal Seminar May 16-19.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:39 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the to Tuesday, April 23, 2024, at 7:00 p.m. for
the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Velveth Schmitz, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 9, 2024
